title: Tenant priority fencing and surplus delegation protocol for burst lanes
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Problem: During short, high-concurrency spikes we allow burst lanes (temporary capacity) but tenants with reserved capacity can be starved or receive unpredictable overage charges. We need a protocol that enforces tenant priority fencing while allowing safe delegation of unused reserved headroom to other tenants (surplus delegation) and produces clear, auditable billing behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Priority fencing: a tenant with active reserved lanes can opt into strict fencing (no borrowable headroom) or soft fencing (borrowable with pre-defined priority and repayment rules).
Surplus delegation: unused reserved capacity can be delegated to a pool for lower-priority tenants under configurable policies (time-to-live, delegate rate, max-delegated-per-tenant).
Arbitration algorithm: implement a fair arbitration that considers tenant priority, recent usage, and repayment debt; documented with complexity O(log N) for scheduling decisions.
Billing attribution: every delegated token is annotated with source tenant, delegation TTL, and a cost attribution tag so invoices and usage UI show origin of burst consumption.

Invoice smoothing: for delegated usage, system produces an 'amortized credit' row that can be toggled in billing exports and account UI; defaults must avoid surprise immediate overage spikes for customers.
Observability: console dashboard shows delegated pool size, per-tenant delegated inflow/outflow, arbitration decisions (top 10 decisions), and SLO impacts.
E2E tests: integration tests that simulate 50 tenants, burst traffic shaped as 99th percentile requests, validate arbitration outcomes and correct invoice line items.
implementation_notes: Admission layer: extend the existing surge admission controller to accept delegation metadata (source_tenant, ttl_seconds, delegate_rate).
Token model: represent delegation as tokens with provenance; tokens decay after TTL and reconciliation job reclaims unused tokens back to source tenant or marks them as expired for billing.
Arbitrator: new component 'burst-arbitrator' that runs in the control plane; uses a priority queue keyed by (priority_score, last_repayment_time) and enforces max-delegated-per-tenant.
Billing pipeline: add tags to metering records for delegated tokens and a post-processing job that computes amortized credits and produces a CSV export for accounting.
Console: add a tenant-level toggle for fencing policy (STRICT | SOFT) and a Surge > Delegation page for operators to view/override active delegations.
Safety: default policy is SAFE-BORROW (no delegation from tenants with active strict SLA flag). Make opt-in required for delegation on enterprise contracts.
Rollout plan: dark launch delegations in staging, enable monitoring-only mode in canary region for 48h, then opt-in for pilot customers (3 customers) before global rollout.
Migration: for existing reserved pools, run a one-time scan to annotate currently unused capacity as candidate-for-delegation but do not auto-delegate without customer opt-in.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: surprise tenant charges if delegation attribution or amortization is incorrect. Mitigation: conservative default (no immediate billing), billing tag audit logs, and manual rollback path in console.
Risk: arbitration fairness bugs could starve low-priority tenants. Mitigation: integrate synthetic fairness tests into CI and run nightly long-tail fair-share simulations.
Risk: increased control-plane load. Mitigation: ensure arbitrator is horizontally scalable and add circuit-breaker to limit delegation decisions per-second.
